concerns.question: The vocabulary captures the three-factor conjunction but does not determine the case-dependent legal classifications underlying its inputs. In particular, the contextual qualifications concerning business activity remain external to business and hong_kong.

The vocabulary cannot distinguish necessary conditions for an ultimate licensing obligation from an exhaustive sufficient legal test. That distinction does not change the selected antecedent and must not be resolved by treating its Boolean result as a complete licensing verdict.
Does the incorporated Circular or Ordinance impose additional conditions beyond the selected three-factor antecedent? Those materials are not supplied, and their effect is outside this predicate.

The three Boolean inputs encode classification outcomes, not the underlying case facts, Type 9 carve-out criteria, or the defeasible force of 'should not in the ordinary course'. Their adequacy depends on external professional judgment.

The vocabulary cannot distinguish joint necessity from legal sufficiency or encode additional requirements from the incorporated Circular and Ordinance. That unresolved distinction does not change the selected antecedent.

The link between the services, the business providing them, and the location of that same business must be preserved when supplying inputs; the Boolean vocabulary cannot independently verify that linkage.
